newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to clear Boeing deal in principle - EU sources.
newsitem.headline: EU to clear Boeing deal in principle - EU sources.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to clear the merger between Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas in principle later on Wednesday, EU sources said. "I believe we will have a decision in principle...subject to verification of the details at a later stage," one source said. Another source said that the concessions made by Boeing in a last-minute proposal on Tuesday were "significant" and that the Commission was likely to give its approval to the $15 billion merger. "There will be no formal decision today, the aim is to approve it politically," a third source said, adding that the formal decision would come in several days.
Earlier, an EU source said Boeing had proposed scrapping its exclusive supply pacts with three airlines in an effort to win EU regulatory approval for the merger.
Boeing's pacts with AMR Corp's American Airlines, Continental Airlines and Delta Air Lines have been one of the major stumbling blocks in talks between the two sides.
Edith Cresson, the French commissioner in charge of research, hinted as she arrived for the Commission's weekly meeting that she would resist clearing the deal despite the last-minute offer.
"That doesn't change at all the heart of the problem," she told Reuters.
Another commissioner, Sweden's Anita Gradin, was more upbeat. "I'm sure," she said, when asked whether there would be a deal.
Other commissioners were more cautious. "I don't know, we will have to discuss it," Commission President Jacques Santer said.
The commissioners were expected to be briefed on Boeing's proposals, submitted by fax on Tuesday afternoon, before starting their regular weekly meeting at 0900/0700 GMT.
